bullets.title: AVGO drops 13-15% AH: AI semis guidance misses elevated buy-side expectations
bullets.body: Broadcom beat Q2 revenue ($22.19B vs $22.13B est) and guided Q3 to $29.4B (above $28.25B est), but Q3 AI semiconductor guidance of $16B missed buy-side expectations of ~$17-17.5B, and FY27 AI revenue was reiterated at '>$100B' vs. the market's hoped-for raise. Bookings exceeded $30B vs. $10.8B shipped, and management guided 10GW shipments in FY27 weighted to 2H. Macquarie downgraded to Neutral ($437 PT); Citi and Wolfe reiterate Buy, calling the pullback a buying opportunity with FY28 visibility improving and capacity secured through 2028-2029 for Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta.

bullets.title: Semis/networking sector down 6-15% in sympathy with AVGO guidance
bullets.body: The AVGO miss dragged MU -7.2%, ARM -7.1%, MRVL -6.7%, ANET -6.7%, CIEN -8-9%, and the SMH was already up 77-99% YTD heading into earnings. Multiple brokers note this is a tactical take-profit event after a 45-day, near-100% semi index run rather than a fundamental inflection, and pullbacks are expected to be bought by underweight investors. Only 58% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-day MA despite the index near ATH, signaling narrowing breadth.

bullets.title: TSMC CEO confirms multi-year chip supply shortfall; CoPoS advanced packaging on pilot line
bullets.body: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei stated that global chip supply will fall short of AI-fueled demand for years even as new US capacity comes online, and reiterated >30% full-year 2026 revenue growth. He confirmed a CoPoS advanced packaging pilot line with volume expected to ramp significantly over 2-3 years, confirmed purchase of High-NA EUV (R&D only, not production-economic yet), and said Taiwan's competitive position will be 'difficult to challenge.' TSMC is targeting 30% US allocation for sub-2nm capacity but cites construction worker shortages.

bullets.title: S&P 500 snaps 9-day winning streak; markets re-price Fed toward hikes
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed down 0.68% (7,557.87), Nasdaq -0.87%, Dow -1.04% on June 3 as ADP payrolls beat at 122K (highest since Jan 2025) and Dallas Fed's Logan said rate hikes later in 2026 'may be warranted.' Futures markets swung from pricing ~50bp of cuts (Feb 2026) to ~20bp of hikes by Dec 2026. The Beige Book flagged strengthening inflation pressures across most districts with softening consumer spending. SPY net gamma flipped negative to -$3B.

bullets.title: Oil rises to $96 WTI, $97.81 Brent on Middle East escalation; Hormuz/Lebanon ceasefire fragile
bullets.body: WTI settled at $96.02/bbl (+2.41%) and Brent at $97.81/bbl after US-Iran military exchanges near Hormuz and Kuwait airport. A Lebanon-Israel ceasefire was announced (conditional on Hezbollah halt) but Jefferies' geopolitical team flagged the deal as fragile and the risk as escalating from single-chokepoint to multi-chokepoint (Hormuz + Bab el-Mandeb). Piper Sandler sees oil averaging $125/bbl in Q3 if Hormuz stays closed. Novak noted global oil market hasn't fully priced Middle East risk and 12M bpd is off market. US crude stockpiles hit 22-year lows.

bullets.title: US effective tariff rate has quietly fallen to 6.8%; new Section 301 tariffs loom
bullets.body: Wolfe DC Policy notes the US effective tariff rate dropped from 10.9% peak (Oct 2025) to 6.8% in March 2026 driven by SCOTUS IEEPA ruling, policy changes on China/India, and tariff evasion. AI-driven capex and OBBB consumer tax cuts are untouched. A new Section 301 proposal is pending, with a 'floor' rate expected followed by higher country-level tariffs, implying modest renewed headwinds in late 2026 but unlikely to derail growth. Semiconductor imports have surged in both volume and price.

bullets.title: Alphabet closes $85B equity offering multiple times oversubscribed; Berkshire joins
bullets.body: Alphabet increased its equity offering from $80B to $85B on heavy demand, closing multiple times oversubscribed. Berkshire Hathaway's participation is seen as a strong validation of Google's AI strategy and marks a shift in AI funding from private to public markets. UBS remains bullish on hyperscaler stocks as distribution engines for Anthropic and OpenAI, seeing Street understating revenue upside. Goldman raised combined hyperscaler capex (GOOGL/META/MSFT/AMZN) forecast to $5.3T for 2025-2030 from $4.5T.

bullets.title: BOJ expected to hike at June meeting; JGB yields rise across the curve
bullets.body: Bloomberg sources indicate the BOJ is mulling a June rate hike with another possible in 2026, while also leaning toward easing its bond-buying reduction pace from fiscal 2027. 10-year JGB yields rose to 2.67%, 20-year to 3.575%. The Korean won hit its weakest level since 2009 vs. USD on KOSPI volatility after AVGO dragged Asian tech lower; South Korea's finance minister pledged market oversight to contain volatility.

bullets.title: Tech sector P/E at 48x (up from 32x since March 30); call option buying at 2021 mania levels
bullets.body: The S&P Tech sector's trailing 12-month P/E jumped from ~32x to 48x since the March 30 low, and tech stocks outperformed the rest of the market by 33% over 3 months (largest margin in history). The 3x Semiconductor ETF is up 1,550% YoY. Call option buying reached 2021 meme-stock era extremes. BTIG, Bespoke, and Jefferies all flagged historical extremes; only 58% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-day MA. NDX weekly RSI hit its highest since the first post-Covid squeeze.

bullets.title: SpaceX prices IPO at $135/share; $1.75T valuation, $75B raise
bullets.body: SpaceX filed its S-1/A and priced 555.56M Class A shares at $135 fixed price (~$75B raise) for NASDAQ listing under SPCX, with pricing expected June 11 post-close. Proceeds targeted at AI compute infrastructure, launch vehicles, and satellite constellation expansion. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Citi, and JPMorgan are bookrunners. Goldman's Waldron said the market has strong absorption capacity for large IPOs.

bullets.title: Anthropic selects Morgan Stanley and Goldman to lead IPO; private credit funds face redemption limits
bullets.body: Anthropic has retained Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs (with JPMorgan participating) to lead IPO preparations. Separately, Partners Group is capping withdrawals on its flagship US PE fund as private credit funds hit redemption limits from surging withdrawal demand. Moody's flagged $662B in AI data-center funding risk; Apollo is shopping a large Anthropic debt deal.

bullets.title: Fed Beige Book: inflation pressures strengthening; K-shaped consumer stress deepening
bullets.body: The June Beige Book showed economic activity expanding at a slight-to-moderate pace in 10 of 12 districts, but inflation pressures strengthened across most districts. Middle-income households are 'squeezing more life' out of budgets and delaying discretionary spending; low-income consumers face heightened financial strain. Business uncertainty remains elevated, and employment was largely flat.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Kumo AI for $400M+; RTX Spark targets consumer AI market
bullets.body: NVIDIA acquired Kumo AI (enterprise foundation models for business predictions) for over $400M. NVIDIA also launched RTX Spark, targeting the local/consumer AI market and competing directly with Apple, Intel, and AMD. Jensen Huang made Foxconn his first Computex stop as Vera Rubin compute trays enter mass production at 1/minute on fully automated lines. Morgan Stanley raised NVDA PT to $288.

bullets.title: PLTR-Google Cloud multi-tiered partnership announced; complements Anthropic not competes
bullets.body: Palantir announced a multi-tiered partnership with Google Cloud including two-way data federation between BigQuery and Foundry, Foundry Ontology and Google Knowledge Catalog semantic exchange, and Palantir Marketplace availability. Multiple brokers note PLTR's Ontology is differentiated vs. Anthropic for complex customized workloads—the two are complementary. PLTR gained 2%+ on the news.

bullets.title: Software/SaaS outperforms semis; valuation at 2016 lows vs. expanded AI monetization
bullets.body: Citi's software universe trades at 24x NTM EV/FCF (ex-SBC), in-line with 2016 lows, while the sector recovered +25% QTD vs. S&P +16%. AI monetization is beginning to drive adoption in agentic platforms, orchestration, and data infrastructure. Wolfe's All-SaaS index saw +7.1% week-over-week multiple expansion. ADBE, CRM, NOW, INTU, TEAM all gained 2-2.4% as software names bid up relative to semis post-AVGO.

bullets.title: EM tech outperformance led by Korea (+35%) and Taiwan (+16.5%) in May on AI trade
bullets.body: MSCI EM gained 9.5% in May, outperforming DM (+4.4%) on AI trade resurgence; EM IT sector is up 89% YTD accounting for more than all of EM's 24.8% YTD gain (ex-IT EM is down -1.1%). Korea's KOSPI rally generated W1 quadrillion (~$700B) in household wealth, with JPM modeling a W14-43T consumption uplift. Asia hedge funds posted +10.2% in May (2nd strongest month in a decade). Japan positioning is stretched to 100th percentile.

bullets.title: Global share buybacks hit $533B in Apr-May, strongest two-month pace on record
bullets.body: JPMorgan data shows global buyback announcements hit $533B in April-May 2026, up from $487B a year prior, driven by US Tech cash flows growing 25% vs. 20% capex growth. Despite Alphabet's $85B equity offering and incoming IPOs, net equity supply for 2026 is projected to rise only modestly (~$200B) given buyback strength, providing technical support to equities.

bullets.title: US broadband market intensely competitive; AT&T best positioned as FWA/fiber leader
bullets.body: UBS sees the US broadband market with no signs of competitive relief: FWA on track to reach ~20M subscribers (~15% of market) by year-end, AT&T targeting 4M+ new fiber passings/yr toward 60M+ by 2030, and cable facing structural headwinds of ~1.7M subscriber losses in 2026. Cable ARPU declines are worsening; Comcast showed temporary improvement from Olympics promos. AT&T positioned as largest converged wireless/fiber operator; T-Mobile attractive on valuation.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler: Core inflation tracking toward 2% by year-end on M2/outlays deceleration
bullets.body: Piper Sandler maintains its 2% core inflation by year-end call, citing M2 deceleration, slowing unit labor costs, and rising productivity. Exogenous shocks (oil, fertilizer) act as demand-destroying taxes in low M2/outlays environment. The World Cup (mid-June to mid-July) poses transient inflation risk via hotel, airline, and restaurant costs. Bessent characterized May inflation as a 'short-term blip,' while Logan flagged trimmed mean may be understating price pressures.

bullets.title: Data center supply: >60% of 2027 planned capacity not yet under construction; power bottleneck intensifying
bullets.body: Over 60% of data center capacity planned for 2027 completion has not yet broken ground, raising execution risks. Public opposition to data centers swung 49 points negative in 9 months (71% now opposed). Power availability, permitting, and electrical infrastructure are increasingly the binding constraints on deployment. Morgan Stanley's NAREIT takeaways confirm EQIX and DLR as beneficiaries; EQIX maintains ~25% cash-on-cash returns with plans to roughly double capacity over 5 years.
